title: Turn from the first to second reset sweep
statement: Let $S$ be a deterministic machine, $A$ a nondeterministic machine, and $x$ a Boolean input word; let $m\in\mathbb N$, let $b$ be a choice bit, and choose an input-head position and work-tape contents and head positions for both machines. One host-machine step from phase $p0$ with yard-tape head at $-1$ moves the input head left with clamping, advances each of $A$’s work-tape heads by one, moves the yard-tape head to $0$, and changes the phase to $p1$, leaving all tape contents, the $S$ work-tape head positions, and the output unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a deterministic machine over Boolean symbols
$A$ is a nondeterministic machine over Boolean symbols
$sT$ and $aT$ specify Boolean work-tape contents for $S$ and $A$
$sP$ and $aP$ specify integer work-tape head positions for $S$ and $A$
